strengths: Insightful motivation: The paper provides a clear and well-substantiated analysis of why standard MoE designs struggle on visual diffusion models, highlighting the fundamental differences between text and visual tokens (high spatial redundancy and functional heterogeneity due to CFG).

Tailored and principled design: The two-step router is nicely customized for diffusion transformers: conditional routing naturally separates conditional and null-conditioned tokens, while prototypical routing combined with the routing contrastive loss (RCL) explicitly optimizes for intra-expert coherence and inter-expert diversity.

Strong empirical performance: Across both Rectified Flow and DDPM training frameworks and various model scales (from Small to XL), ProMoE consistently and significantly outperforms dense DiTs (at matched activated parameters) as well as existing diffusion MoE baselines (DiT-MoE, EC-DiT, DiffMoE).

Comprehensive experimental analysis: The paper includes thorough ablations (routing activations, individual components, loss weights, load balancing interaction) and scaling studies (varying both model size and expert counts), along with informative t-SNE and singular-value subspace similarity visualizations.
weaknesses: Evaluation scope is limited to ImageNet class-conditional generation: Modern DiT scaling is largely motivated by high-resolution text-to-image generation (e.g., SD3, Flux, PixArt). Demonstrating whether this explicit guidance translates equally well to multimodal text-conditioned settings would significantly strengthen the paper's impact.

Lack of wall-clock speed and inference latency benchmarks: Although the method matches activated parameter counts and theoretical FLOPs of dense baselines, MoE architectures often incur practical hardware overhead (e.g., memory bandwidth, dispatching/all-to-all communication overhead). Reporting actual throughput (training samples/sec and sampling latency) is important for practical adoption.

Distributed execution details for RCL: In Eq. (6), the routing contrastive loss computes expert centroids within a mini-batch. It is somewhat unclear how centroids are aggregated across multi-node/multi-GPU distributed data parallel (DDP) setups, or whether potential expert starvation during early iterations poses stability issues.

strengths: Well-motivated diagnosis of why MoE underperforms in Diffusion Transformers compared to LLMs, supported by insightful empirical analyses on visual token redundancy and functional heterogeneity.

The proposed ProMoE architecture is neat and specifically tailored to diffusion models: partitioning conditional and unconditional tokens effectively addresses CFG characteristics, while prototypical routing provides a principled foundation for latent semantic allocation.
The Routing Contrastive Loss (RCL) elegantly addresses both intra-expert coherence and inter-expert diversity, serving as a semantically grounded alternative to conventional load-balancing losses.

Solid empirical results across both DDPM and Rectified Flow paradigms, demonstrating consistent improvements over dense DiTs and existing MoE baselines (DiT-MoE, EC-DiT, DiffMoE) across various model scales (B, L, XL).
Thorough ablation studies verifying each component, including the router activation function, routing contrastive learning, conditional routing, and scaling behavior.
weaknesses: Evaluation is restricted to class-conditional ImageNet generation at 256x256. Demonstrating the method on text-to-image generation (e.g., using T5/CLIP text conditioning) would significantly strengthen the claim that this routing framework generalizes well across diverse diffusion paradigms.

Lack of actual wall-clock throughput and inference latency measurements. In MoE systems, dispatch overhead, conditional branching, and gather/scatter operations can introduce non-trivial hardware latency that parameter counts alone do not reflect.

The batch-level centroid computation in the routing contrastive loss (Eq. 6) inherently depends on the batch size and token diversity per mini-batch. A sensitivity analysis regarding batch size during training is absent.

strengths: Clear and well-motivated premise: The paper provides insightful analysis contrasting language tokens with visual diffusion tokens, specifically identifying high spatial redundancy and functional heterogeneity (caused by classifier-free guidance) as key obstacles to expert specialization in DiT-MoE architectures.

Principled and coherent technical design: The two-step routing framework is logically structured—conditional routing cleanly segregates unconditional and conditional representations, while prototypical routing combined with the routing contrastive loss (RCL) provides an unsupervised mechanism to encourage intra-expert coherence and inter-expert diversity.

Solid empirical results across architectures and objectives: The method is validated on both Rectified Flow and DDPM objectives across multiple model scales (Base, Large, XL), consistently outperforming dense DiT counterparts and recent vision MoE baselines (DiT-MoE, EC-DiT, DiffMoE) under comparable parameter budgets.

Thorough ablation studies and visual analyses: The submission provides systematic ablations covering each module, the activation functions, the routing contrastive weight, and load-balancing dynamics, supported by informative t-SNE representations of expert-token assignments.
weaknesses: Limited dataset and task diversity: The experimental validation is restricted exclusively to class-conditional image generation on ImageNet-1K (256x256). It remains unclear how well this design generalizes to text-to-image synthesis, where conditioning is more complex and open-ended than discrete class labels.

Lack of wall-clock efficiency and hardware latency profiling: Although the paper properly matches the number of activated parameters and theoretical compute, MoE architectures often incur practical hardware overheads (e.g., dynamic dispatch, memory footprint, and kernel fragmentation). Reporting actual training step times and inference throughput (samples/sec) would provide a complete assessment of practical utility.

Underexplored routing behavior across diffusion timesteps: Diffusion models exhibit dramatically different semantic properties at high-noise versus low-noise timesteps. While the authors demonstrate overall expert diversity, a deeper analysis into how token dispatching interacts with the diffusion time schedule would strengthen the study.

Analysis of expert load and stability: The paper claims that RCL's push-away mechanism naturally balances expert loads, but it lacks detailed quantitative tracking (e.g., expert load variance or token overflow rates over the course of training) to confirm the absence of routing collapse under diverse initialization seeds.

strengths: Insightful analysis of the fundamental differences between language and visual tokens in the context of MoE, pinpointing spatial redundancy and functional heterogeneity (stemming from classifier-free guidance) as primary causes of poor expert specialization in DiTs.

Well-designed and conceptually elegant architectural solution (ProMoE): decoupling conditional and unconditional computation via dedicated unconditional experts, combined with prototypical routing and a Routing Contrastive Loss (RCL) that promotes intra-expert coherence and inter-expert diversity.

Convincing empirical performance across both modern Rectified Flow and DDPM objectives on ImageNet 256x256, consistently outperforming both dense DiT counterparts and recent DiT-MoE baselines (DiT-MoE, EC-DiT, DiffMoE) under matched activation budgets.
Remarkable parameter efficiency: ProMoE-L achieves better generative performance (FID / IS) than dense DiT-XL despite utilizing significantly fewer activated parameters.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation and ablations, including scaling studies across model sizes (Base to XL), expert numbers, training trajectories up to 2M steps, activation functions, and preliminary validation on text-to-image generation with GenEval.
weaknesses: Text-to-image evaluation is relatively lightweight, trained on a small 2M-image subset of LAION-5B; evaluating on larger datasets (e.g., full LAION, CC12M) or higher resolutions would further solidify the claims in open-domain text-to-image generation.

Training overhead and distributed scaling considerations: Table 14 shows training time essentially doubles in GPU hours compared to dense DiTs (333.33 vs. 166.67 GPU hours), but the paper lacks an in-depth analysis of distributed communication overhead (e.g., All-to-All communication latency and memory footprint during distributed expert dispatch).

The conditioning dropout rate in CFG training typically exposes the unconditional expert to only 10-20% of the training tokens. A deeper discussion on the training dynamics, sample efficiency, and gradient variance of the unconditional expert under such data imbalance would improve completeness.

strengths: Clear problem formulation and insightful analysis: The paper pinpoints key differences between language and visual tokens in MoE architectures—namely high spatial redundancy and CFG-induced functional heterogeneity—supported by intuitive empirical analyses (e.g., inter-to-intra class distance ratios and subspace similarity).

Principled and well-integrated design: The proposed ProMoE framework directly addresses these core challenges through a two-step routing scheme. Conditional routing cleanly separates conditional and unconditional processing roles under CFG, while prototypical routing with the Routing Contrastive Loss (RCL) provides an effective unsupervised clustering objective that enforces intra-expert coherence, inter-expert diversity, and semantic load balancing without external labels.

Extensive and rigorous experimental validation: The method is evaluated across multiple model scales (S, B, L, XL), under both DDPM and Rectified Flow formulations, and extended to 2M training steps. ProMoE consistently and significantly outperforms dense DiT counterparts as well as prior MoE diffusion baselines (DiT-MoE, EC-DiT, DiffMoE) at matched or reduced activated parameter counts.

Broad evaluation including text-to-image: Beyond class-conditional ImageNet generation, the authors validate the framework on text-to-image generation using an MM-DiT architecture evaluated on GenEval, demonstrating good generalization across generative modalities.

Thorough ablations and efficiency analysis: The submission contains detailed ablation studies dissecting every design choice (prototypical routing, RCL, conditional routing, activation functions, comparison with conventional load-balancing and GMMs) and provides transparent reporting of GFLOPs and wall-clock inference speed.
weaknesses: Dependency on batch statistics for Routing Contrastive Loss: The centroids in RCL are computed per mini-batch over tokens dispatched to each expert. While effective with standard diffusion batch sizes, performance sensitivity under smaller batch sizes or gradient accumulation setups could be more thoroughly discussed.

Unconditional expert utilization during standard inference: In inference settings where classifier-free guidance is omitted (cfg = 1.0), the unconditional experts remain unutilized, leading to a discrepancy in active capacity compared to CFG-guided sampling.

Scale of text-to-image validation: The text-to-image experiment is conducted on a 2M subset of LAION-5B, which is sufficient as a proof-of-concept for academic resources, but leaves performance on massive web-scale multi-modal pretraining as an open question.

strengths: Clear motivation and insightful analysis: The paper identifies key differences between language and vision tokens (spatial redundancy and functional heterogeneity under classifier-free guidance) that hinder expert specialization in DiT MoEs, providing a convincing rationale for explicit routing guidance.

Well-designed technical approach: The proposed two-step routing framework is elegant. Hard conditional routing effectively addresses the functional dichotomy between conditional and unconditional tokens, while prototypical routing with Routing Contrastive Loss (RCL) provides label-free semantic guidance that promotes intra-expert coherence and inter-expert diversity without requiring traditional auxiliary load-balancing losses.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: The authors conduct extensive experiments across multiple training objectives (Rectified Flow and DDPM), model scales (Small to XL), training durations (up to 2M steps), and tasks (ImageNet class-conditional and LAION text-to-image). Comparisons against competitive MoE baselines (DiT-MoE, EC-DiT, DiffMoE) consistently demonstrate superior generative performance (FID, IS, GenEval) at matched activated parameters and comparable computational cost.

Thorough ablation and analytical studies: The paper provides convincing ablation studies dissecting each component (conditional routing, prototypical routing, RCL, activation functions), expert utilization analysis via t-SNE, and scaling behaviors across both model sizes and expert counts.
weaknesses: Limited exploration on text-to-image scale: The text-to-image experiments are restricted to a 2M-image subset of LAION-5B. While understandable due to computational constraints, evaluating on larger and more diverse datasets would further validate generalization to large-scale foundation model training.

Deeper analysis on score activation is lacking: The finding that the identity function outperforms sigmoid and softmax for mapping latent similarities into routing scores is somewhat counterintuitive; further analysis or visualization regarding score distribution dynamics would strengthen this discussion.

Handling of negative prompts / CFG variants in T2I: The conditional vs. unconditional token separation assumes standard CFG (conditioning vs. null conditioning). More discussion on how this adapts to arbitrary negative prompting in text-to-image settings would be beneficial.
